# openai_external_key (Resource)

Registers a customer-managed encryption key for Enterprise Key Management (EKM). Activate it on a project by setting the project's `external_key_id`. EKM is only available on certain accounts. Refer to the [EKM (External Keys) in the Management API](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20000953-ekm-external-keys-in-the-management-api) article. The API does not support updates, so changing any argument replaces the key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A key in Google Cloud KMS. Use `aws` or `azure` instead for keys in AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault.
resource "openai_external_key" "example" {
  name = "Example EKM key"

  gcp = {
    workload_identity_project_number = "123456789012"
    workload_identity_pool_id        = "openai-pool"
    workload_identity_provider_id    = "openai-provider"
    audience                         = "org-000000000000000000000000"
    kms_project_id                   = "example-kms-project"
    kms_key_ring_name                = "openai"
    kms_key_name                     = "openai-ekm"
    kms_key_location                 = "us"
  }
}

# Encrypt a project's data with the key.
resource "openai_project" "example" {
  name            = "Example Project"
  external_key_id = openai_external_key.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) A friendly name for the external key.

### Optional

- `aws` (Attributes) A key in AWS KMS. Exactly one of `aws`, `azure` or `gcp` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--aws))
- `azure` (Attributes) A key in Azure Key Vault. Exactly one of `aws`, `azure` or `gcp` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure))
- `gcp` (Attributes) A key in Google Cloud KMS, accessed through Workload Identity Federation. Exactly one of `aws`, `azure` or `gcp` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--gcp))

### Read-Only

- `api_project_ids` (Set of String) The IDs of the projects that use this key.
- `created_at` (Number) The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the key was registered.
- `id` (String) The ID of the external key.

<a id="nestedatt--aws"></a>
### Nested Schema for `aws`

Required:

- `external_id` (String) The external ID OpenAI presents when assuming the role: your organization ID or project ID.
- `kms_arn` (String) The ARN of the KMS key.
- `role_arn` (String) The ARN of the IAM role OpenAI assumes in your account.


<a id="nestedatt--azure"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure`

Required:

- `key_name` (String) The name of the key in the Key Vault.
- `tenant_id` (String) The Microsoft Entra tenant ID.
- `vault_uri` (String) The URI of the Key Vault that holds the key.


<a id="nestedatt--gcp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `gcp`

Required:

- `audience` (String) The audience OpenAI uses when exchanging tokens with the Workload Identity provider. It must be one of the provider's allowed audiences.
- `kms_key_location` (String) The location of the key ring, such as `us` or `europe-west1`.
- `kms_key_name` (String) The name of the key.
- `kms_key_ring_name` (String) The name of the key ring.
- `kms_project_id` (String) The ID of the Google Cloud project that holds the key ring.
- `workload_identity_pool_id` (String) The ID of the Workload Identity pool.
- `workload_identity_project_number` (String) The number of the Google Cloud project that holds the Workload Identity pool.
- `workload_identity_provider_id` (String) The ID of the Workload Identity provider registered for OpenAI.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing external key
terraform import openai_external_key.example <external_key_id>

# Example
terraform import openai_external_key.example extkey_000000000000000000000000
```
